messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: p99 tail latency for streaming API > 1.5s across AZs (model=gpt-small-v1). Source: cross-zone TLS handshake spikes, triggered 2026-03-15T11:02:57Z :rotating_light:

alice (oncall): seeing it in the console, p95 also creeping up. paging now. oncall here, I'll triage.

carol (sre): I'm pulling traces, looks like a TLS SYN/handshake retry storm between az-b and az-c egress NATs. lots of retransmits in the handshake stage.

bob (neteng): confirmed - increased SYN retransmit counters on the nat-egress pods in az-c. DNS lookups look fine. packetloss on the crosszone path ~1-2% during spike windows.

dave (eng-runtime): streaming stalls are from the initial TLS setup delaying the first few bytes -> KV cache warmups get dragged. clients see p99 jumps ~1.8-2s.

alice (oncall): customer impact? any active customers seeing errors or disconnects?

eva (product-support): a few power users reported stalls and reconnects, 2 support tickets opened (CS-3421, CS-3422). I'll assemble the customer list.

frank (redwood-monitor): metrics: 
- p95 tokens latency: 420ms -> 620ms
- p99 tokens latency: 1.2s -> 2.1s
- TLS handshake time (median): 120ms -> 980ms
- retransmits/s on nat-egress-azc: 0.8 -> 14.6

carol (sre): initial mitigation options: 1) route streaming traffic to same-AZ egress (avoid cross-zone NAT) 2) temporarily increase handshake timeout and allow session reuse 3) enable fallback to a lighter model variant for affected routes 4) scale nat-egress replicas to reduce queueing

bob (neteng): routing change is low-risk if we can pin pods by AZ. I can push a selective route policy: `route-policy set --src=pods/streaming --prefer-local-egress` will bias to local NAT. Doing a dry-run now.

alice (oncall): go for it, prefer-local looks good. Carol, can you coordinate traffic shift? Dave, be ready to rollback model/route changes.

bob (neteng): dry-run succeeded on staging. Applying to prod for region eu-west2 first.

incident-bot: ACTION: route-policy change by bob applied to eu-west2 at 11:12 UTC. Monitoring.

carol (sre): metrics update after routing change (2m): TLS handshake p99 -> 410ms, p99 tokens latency -> 760ms, retransmits down to 2.1/s. Partial improvement.

alice (oncall): good. continue rollout to us-west. Eva, flag impacted customers and send interim note: "we're seeing intermittent streaming stalls; rolling mitigation in progress".

eva (product-support): will do. draft: "We're mitigating increased streaming tail latency caused by cross-AZ networking handshakes. We've applied a temporary routing change and are monitoring. We will follow up with RCA." sending now.

dave (eng-runtime): deployed a quick tweak to enable session resumption TTL increase for streaming agent (config: `tls.session_ttl=3600s`) to reduce full handshakes. Deployed canary to 10% of streaming servers.

carol (sre): can we also throttle connect retries in the client lib? double retry backoff would reduce retransmit pressure.

alice (oncall): good idea, file a patch and prod rollout after validation. Not now if it's risky.

frank (redwood-monitor): post-rollout metrics (10m): p99 handshake -> 280ms, p99 tokens latency -> 540ms, retransmits ~0.6/s. Impact appears mitigated in eu-west2 and us-west1 where routing applied.

bob (neteng): rolling routing change to remaining regions now (applied us-west1 at 11:28, ap-southeast in progress). No config drift.

incident-bot: NOTE: on-call handoff scheduled. alice -> carol at 12:00 UTC for follow-through and RCA.

carol (sre): taking handoff. I'll keep the routing policy in place until we finish root-cause. Next steps for RCA: collect tcpdump on nat-egress nodes, correlate with cloud provider inter-AZ path metrics, check kernel conntrack exhaustion, and review any recent NAT image updates.

bob (neteng): starting tcpdump on nat-egress-azc (pcap saved to s3://redwood-dumps/2153337777/nat-egress-azc.pcap). Command: `sudo tcpdump -i eth0 -w /tmp/handshake-dump.pcap 'tcp[tcpflags] & (tcp-syn) != 0'`

dave (eng-runtime): noting a recent change from 3 weeks ago: we enabled ephemeral port reuse optimization in nat-agent v1.12.0. Will validate if that interacts badly with provider NAT.

carol (sre): early pcap inspection: lots of SYN, SYN-ACK pairs but delayed ACKs and retransmits after ~200ms. Provider-side retransmit counters also show occasional queue scheduling spikes.

bob (neteng): opening a ticket with provider (CLOUD-8791) to check intra-region inter-AZ fabric for packet copies/queueing.

alice (oncall): customer-facing status updated. mitigation = routing to local-egress + session resumption TTL increase. No widespread errors. Keep monitoring and prepare postmortem.

frank (redwood-monitor): alert thresholds auto-snoozed for this incident. I'll keep long-running dashboards pinned to the channel.

eva (product-support): contacting top 5 affected customers with workaround tips (reconnect less aggressively, set client session reuse).

carol (sre): postmortem action items (quick list):
- NetEng: provider follow-up and packet path analysis (owner: bob)
- Runtime: validate nat-agent v1.12 interaction and roll back or patch if needed (owner: dave)
- SRE: formal RCA and timeline + write customer impact summary (owner: carol)
- Product-support: consolidate customer messages and list of tickets (owner: eva)

alice (oncall): handoff complete. carol, you're oncall for the rest. I'll be available for escalation.

carol (sre): acknowledged. marking incident as mitigated (impact reduced, rolling improvements). Will open incident doc and link to runbook artifacts.

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: mitigated -> watching. Incident channel will remain open for RCA until closed.

bob (neteng): added provider ticket link: https://cloud.provider/tickets/CLOUD-8791. Also captured per-node conntrack stats and NAT queue lengths in S3.

carol (sre): thanks all. saved traces and logs to s3://redwood-incidents/2153337777/. Postmortem draft ETA: 48 hours.

frank (redwood-monitor): leaving a note: consider adding a synthetic that exercises cross-AZ TLS handshakes under load to catch this earlier.

alice (oncall): +1 for synthetic. good find team. :thumbsup:
